title: KS3 / Year 7-9 Science — Physics Magnetism and Electromagnetism
subtitle: Revision pack for magnetic materials, fields, electromagnets, investigations, and applications.

description: A KS3 physics revision pack covering magnetism as a non-contact force, magnetic materials, poles, fields, induced magnetism, electromagnets, practical investigations, and everyday applications. Items emphasise common misconceptions, data handling, fair testing, and clear evidence-based explanations.

data.title: Testing Materials with a Bar Magnet
data.instruction: Put the practical steps in a sensible order.
items: Collect the objects and identify their main materials where possible.
Place one object on the bench away from other magnetic objects.
Bring the bar magnet close to the object without pushing it by hand.
Record whether the object is attracted to the magnet.
Repeat for the other objects using the same method.
Use the results to decide which materials are magnetic in the classroom test.

topics: KS3 Science: Physics Magnetism and Electromagnetism

data.title: Induced Magnetism in a Paperclip Chain
data.instruction: Put the explanation in the correct order.
items: A steel paperclip is placed in the magnetic field of a strong magnet.
The paperclip becomes temporarily magnetised by induction.
The temporary magnetism lets the first paperclip attract another paperclip.
The next paperclip also becomes temporarily magnetised.
A chain of paperclips can hang from the magnet.
When the magnet is removed, most of the temporary magnetism is lost.

topics: KS3 Science: Physics Magnetism and Electromagnetism

data.title: Investigating Coil Turns and Electromagnet Strength
data.instruction: Order the method for a fair test.
items: Wrap 10 turns of insulated wire around the same iron nail.
Connect the coil to the same cell, switch, and leads.
Close the switch for a short fixed time.
Touch the electromagnet to identical paperclips and count how many are lifted.
Open the switch to stop the current and let the coil cool.
Repeat three times, then test 20, 30, 40, and 50 turns.
Calculate the mean number of paperclips lifted for each number of turns.

topics: KS3 Science: Physics Magnetism and Electromagnetism

data.title: Electric Bell Cycle
data.instruction: Put the simple electromagnet bell cycle in order.
items: The switch is closed and current flows through the circuit.
The electromagnet becomes magnetic.
The electromagnet pulls the iron armature.
The movement breaks the electrical contact.
The current stops and the electromagnet switches off.
The armature springs back and remakes the contact.
The cycle repeats quickly, producing a buzzing or ringing sound.
